20 or 10 Exposures
GIL FRIEDBERG
Boston Globe (1960-1979); Jul 25, 1965;
pg. 37

The Camera Eye |
20 or 10 Exposures |

By GIL FRIEDBERG
Camera Editor

It isn't often camera inven-
tions are patented by local
talent, but a new size format,
along with rapid-shift lever
for use in one of the more
popular makes of cameras,
now used by _ professional
news and amateur camera-
men, is on the market.
The new reflex camera at-
tachment, although not perti-
nent to the operation of the
camera, will now give a 2%4x-
2% inch negative instead of
the 2% inch square.
This, said Maurice “Moe”
Reed of Newton Center, its
inventor, will permit the use
of -the new 220 Kodak film
which will make either 20 or
10 exposures out of the origi-
nal 120 size,
The twin-lens reflex cam-
era to which Reed's new at-
tachment accessory is fitted
is not only one of the first
to carry the 20-exposure
magazine that now presents
the proportionate size for a
comfortable 8x10 inch en-
largement, sans cropping, but
it also has a rapid-shift lever
which advances the film in
its convenient cassette — ex-
tra ones can be carried and
quickly inserted in the cam-
era back when needed.
The camera js fitted to take
five lenses of various focal
lengths ranging from 65mm
up to 180mm but the distinct
advantage of this innovation
is still the size and rapidity
in which a quantity of shots
can he made without worry-
ing too much about running
out-of film and having to
change right in the middle of
an important assignment,

A revolutionary step for-
ward in. the business end of
the lens has been perfected.
It is the electronic shutter for
the Compur Lens.

Previously the cocking and
release of these shutters waa
effected by spring power and,
although the leaves of the
shutter seemed to work with
precision-like accuracy, the
timing was dependent on me-
chanical gears,
Now . the performance ‘Is
done by an electromagnet
with a degreee of accuracy
that never before had come
close.
In simple words, the shut-

ter works on a transistorized
circuit which is small enough
to be inserted into the shutter
housing. Speeds.range from
1-200 second yp to 32 full
seconds in 14 marked settings.
The aperture stops can be
set from f4 to £90.

After each exposure, the
shutter resets itself automati-
cally and instantly and the
camera is ready for the next
exposures,

Amazingly, the new elec-
tronic shutter has made cam-
era operation so effective and
convenient that the photogra-
pher no longer has to run
back and forth from front to
rear of camera to change ap-
erture or lens opening.

Now he can observe the
entire workings of his lens
from the focusing screen and
with the necessary cables op-
erate these important facets
from anywhere in the studio. .
‘The new shutters are called
the 5FS and the Electronic 3,
and are the products of Com-
pur Works, Munich.

Fashion editors take note—
‘we may very soon see women
wearing their favorite vaca-
tion snapshots, Ladies’ clothes
are being made of photo-
linen in West Germany. The
linen has g photographic
emulsion: and goes through
the normal process of print-
ing and enlarging,

We may soon see a@ sign
in front of: fashionable’ de-
partment — stores —_ reading
“latest fashions — portraits
of your loved ones printed
on your favorite formal.”

The window of the Work-
ingmen’s Co-operative Bank
at 264 Massachusetts av., Bos-
ton, displays photographs by

Ulrike Welsch of Chestnut gt.,”

Boston,
The exhibit will end July 31.

The brand new sequence
idea of taking successive pic-
tures in rapid order hus now
been glamorized with a new
flash system. It Is the new
multiple flash cube,

The new cube contains four
AGI flash bulbs which : ro-

tate on e# small gear that:

meshes into the top of the

new Kodak Instamatle cam-
era.
- Every. time the film is ad-
vanced . the- cube turns to.
place'a new. bulb ‘toward the
subject. .
In some of the- Instamatie
cameras, a‘ spring ‘is wound
to take up enough slack to
shoot the entire roll of film.
As the shutter.is tripped and
the flash goes off, three things
happen before you can say
“shoot the works” — the film
advances, to the. next number,”
the shutter is cocked and
ready to. go, and the flash
cube turns to place into readi-
ness a fresh bulb,
Four pictures can be taken
in - five seconds, But who
wants to get rid of that many
pictures so quickly?
Hpwever, the new idea of
flash really synchronizes
flash exposures. It also short-
ens the handling period since
the photographer now handles
one object to take four pic-
tures instead of four separate
bulbs.
Maximum distance should
not be over nine feet for
these small bulbs,
The new system is limited
to Instamatic cameras only,
but we see the start of some-
thing really big in the near
future when the idea can be
put to use in other cameras,
+A less-than-§20 Polaroid
camera that makes black and
white pictures in 10 seconds
has just been announced. The
new cameras will be sold in
Canada only starting this
week,

Perhaps late in September
sales will be made in the
United States. You probably
won't believe it, but the new
camera contains a knob
which, when turned, ‘will
change a “no” into a “yes”
only i) the light conditions
say so. Then one just presses
the knob, and the shutter will
go off.
After 10 seconds develop-
ment, a wallet size picture
is made, The lens is a set-
focus type (f96) but ASA
3000-speed film is used. It has
a constant speed shutter of
1-200th . second, There's no
film winding or threading
since the roll is merely
dropped into ‘the back of the
camera, named “The
Swinger.”
